added_meaning: Remaining Senate 100051 purposes (1) through (4), (6), (7) and (12) share the additional $2,055,000,000 fiscal year 2025 appropriation to the Secretary of Homeland Security, available through September 30, 2029. They are purposes within that account, not separate full-envelope earmarks or borrowed ICE/House amounts. The paragraph 1 purpose is hiring and training of additional U.S. Customs and Border Protection agents, and the necessary support staff, to carry out immigration enforcement activities. The paragraph 2 purpose is funding for transportation costs and related costs associated with the departure or removal of aliens. The paragraph 3 purpose is funding for the assignment of Department of Homeland Security employees and State officers to carry out immigration enforcement activities pursuant to sections 103(a) and 287(g) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1103(a) and 1357(g)). The paragraph 4 purpose is hiring additional staff and investing the necessary resources to enhance screening and vetting of all aliens seeking entry into United States, consistent with section 212 of such Act (8 U.S.C. 1182), or intending to remain in the United States, consistent with section 237 of such Act (8 U.S.C. 1227). The paragraph 6 purpose is transporting and facilitating the return, pursuant to section 235(b)(2)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1225(b)(2)(C)), of aliens arriving from contiguous territory. The paragraph 7 purpose is funding for State and local participation in homeland security efforts for purposes of: ending the presence of criminal gangs and criminal organizations throughout the United States; addressing crime and public safety threats; combating human smuggling and trafficking networks throughout the United States; supporting immigration enforcement activities; and providing reimbursement for State and local participation in such efforts. The paragraph 12 purpose is information technology investments to support immigration purposes, including improvements to fee and revenue collections. The entry and intended-remain screening categories retain their own section 212 and section 237 references. The State/local participation list retains all five own purposes, including its own throughout-the-United-States phrases. It does not borrow the reimbursement fund's crime-plus-unlawful-presence category or domestic transport restriction. The general departure/removal transportation purpose prints no separate within-the-United-States phrase. The assignment list retains Department of Homeland Security employees and State officers pursuant to both printed statutory references, not authority for any State employee to exercise all Federal powers. The printed purpose lists do not determine that a particular expenditure must fulfill every listed category. Fee and revenue collection IT is not a new fee, fine or penalty charge. Complete captured 103(a) retains its named agency roles, regulatory/delegation powers, consents and other conditions. In captured 103(a)(10), the Attorney General may authorize a State or local law enforcement officer to perform or exercise any of the powers, privileges, or duties conferred or imposed by this chapter or regulations issued thereunder upon officers or employees of the Service only in the event of the Attorney General's determination that an actual or imminent mass influx of aliens arriving off the coast of the United States, or near a land border, presents urgent circumstances requiring an immediate Federal response, and with the consent of the head of the department, agency, or establishment under whose jurisdiction the individual is serving. The captured event-specific authorization does not establish general unconditioned State power. Previously bound full 287(g) agreement qualifications, training, written powers/duration, Federal direction/supervision, voluntary/communication/cooperation and expense/employment/liability distinctions remain unchanged. Complete captured section 212(a) grounds and remaining operative section 212 authorities retain their own standards, exceptions, discretionary waivers and conditional notice rules, not an every-alien crime finding or guaranteed notice/waiver. January 29, 2025 Public Law 119-1 replaces the original Attorney General references in 212(d)(5) with Secretary of Homeland Security and adds the distinct State enforcement route. Original captured 2024 words are preserved with that amending law, not relabeled as the complete unamended 2025 section. Complete captured section 237 retains distinct deportability grounds, actual conviction/knowledge/timing or other own requirements, exceptions/waivers, special nonimmigrant and SIJ boundaries and conditional administrative stays; screening funding does not determine an individual inadmissible, deportable or criminal. The contiguous-return purpose is pursuant to 235(b)(2)(C). The captured 235(b)(2)(C) return authority concerns an applicant for admission whom the examining immigration officer determines is not clearly and beyond a doubt entitled to be admitted, arriving on land (whether or not at a designated port of arrival) from a foreign territory contiguous to the United States. The Attorney General may return that alien to that territory pending a proceeding under section 1229a. The captured parent exceptions for a crewman, an alien to whom paragraph (1) applies, and a stowaway remain. Discretionary return is not a final removal order or universal cross-border return duty. Complete captured 240 proceedings retain judge/charge/exclusive-procedure exceptions, own representation and evidence/examination limits, burdens, decision/appeal, motion and notice/deadline/stay rules. No guaranteed relief, government-paid counsel or individual hearing/return result is inferred. Other H.R.1 immigration components and separately reserved application questions remain unfinished.
